paragraphs.source_en: When Miss Yukie had said this much, she seemed unable to contain her feelings, and a handful of tears fell streaming onto her purple hakama. The master stared blankly at Yukie's downcast face, as though he were studying what kind of mental process had produced those tears. Just then, Osan the maid came from the kitchen, placed her red hands neatly together beyond the threshold, and said, "A visitor has come to see you." The master asked, "Who has come?" Osan glanced sideways at Yukie's tear-stained face and replied to the master, "It is a student from the school." The master went out to the parlor. I too, for the sake of gathering material and conducting human research, followed after the master and quietly went around to the veranda.

paragraphs.source_en: To study human beings, unless one chooses a moment when some disturbance is taking place, no results will come of it. In ordinary times, ordinary people remain ordinary no matter when one observes them, so what I can see and hear amounts to nothing but ordinary people and ordinary affairs, with no vitality at all. But once an extraordinary situation arises, this ordinariness, driven by some subtle and mysterious force, quickly brings forth all manner of strange, odd, wonderful, and peculiar things; in short, events that greatly broaden the horizons of us cats appear everywhere. Miss Yukie's tears are precisely one of these phenomena. Miss Yukie, possessed of such an inscrutable and immeasurable mind, seemed nothing especially remarkable while chatting with the master's wife; but from the moment the master returned and tossed the oil jar onto the mat, she suddenly displayed a marvelous natural quality, as though air had been pumped into a dead dragon. And that quality is one common to all the women under heaven; it simply does not readily show itself. No, in truth it shows itself at every moment of the twenty-four hours, only it does not appear so plainly, so brilliantly, and so unreservedly as this. Thanks to a particularly perverse eccentric like the master, who is fond of stroking our fur the wrong way, I was able to witness this fine performance. So long as I follow close behind the master, wherever he goes, the actors on the stage are sure to move without knowing it. Having been taken in by such an interesting master, I have been able, within the brief span of a cat's life, to experience a great many things. I am truly grateful. Now then, who might this visitor be?

paragraphs.source_zh: 为了进行对人的研究，假如不选择发生某种波澜的时机，那是不会取得成果的。在平时，平庸的人不管到何时也还是平庸的，所以我所能见到和听到的，无非是一些平庸的人和平庸的事，毫无活力可言。但是，一旦遇到非常情况，这种平庸性，就会受一种灵妙的神秘作用推动，很快就会涌现出许多新奇的、古怪的、美妙的、特异的事物来，简单说吧，对于大益于开拓我们猫儿眼界的许多事件，到处都会出现。雪江姑娘的眼泪，正是这种现象之一。具有如此不可思议、不可捉摸的心理的雪江姑娘，在和主人妻子闲谈的时候，并不使人觉得有什么特异之处，但自从主人回来将油壶扔在铺席上以后，她立刻就像一条死龙用气筒打入空气一样，突然发挥出一种美妙的天生丽质来。而这种丽质是天下妇女所共有的，只不过它不会轻易就显现出来罢了。不，其实在二十四小时中随时都会显现出来，只是不像这样灼然可见、毫不掩饰地表现出来罢了。幸亏有主人这种喜欢摩挲我们猫儿皮毛的、特别执拗的怪人，才使我得以拜见这出好戏。我只要紧跟在主人身后，不论走到哪里，这舞台上的演员就会身不由己地活动起来。我承蒙这位主人收养，使我在这短暂的猫儿的一生当中，体验到这么许多事情，实在感谢。那么这次来的客人又是谁呢？
